fit: stroke synthesis eligibility and separate piperine protocol
assessment: The review lists Rofes among excluded oral piperine comparisons and documents independent capsaicin studies. Its synthesis supplies no cracked-berry or Parkinson swallowing estimate.

fit: piperine in a swallowing review without pain severity assessment
assessment: Piperine is a genuine black-pepper constituent discussed as an isolated swallowing stimulus. No culinary pepper pain measurement was performed.

fit: coffee and caffeine in an adenosine review
assessment: Coffee is part of the epidemiology and mechanism context. The review contains no independent brewed-coffee Parkinson fatigue comparison.

fit: eggs reported in infant feeding interviews
assessment: Parents discuss infant egg introduction and fears of allergies. Preparation and fall frequency were not measured. The source does not involve older adults or Parkinson.

fit: TEAM-AD soybean-oil placebo component identified by review
assessment: Two review sections describe different arms of one TEAM-AD trial. The oil appears as a matching capsule comparator. Fall counts belong to the linked primary report and do not isolate cooking-oil intake.

fit: crocin and crocetin in neuronal cell culture
assessment: Isolated constituents influenced amyloid or tau readouts in cell models. They do not measure depressive symptom severity after whole ground saffron.
The complete brief review distinguishes coffee preparations in liver epidemiology and mentions possible risks. It gives no fatigue or Parkinson beverage comparison.

fit: grape constituents, wine and cancer endpoints
assessment: Grape-related chemistry and wine are direct review topics. No raw grape or separate anxiety comparison in people with Parkinson disease.

fit: olive oil listed in a Mediterranean pattern
assessment: Olive oil is dietary background in an article about wine and cancer. No cold-pressed comparator or anxiety result is reported.

fit: ground Ceylon cinnamon and MPTP motor tests
assessment: The actual Ceylon cinnamon arm used orally administered ground material. Figure 8 reports rotarod and open-field measures. Neither instrument gives separate muscle rigidity severity.

fit: orange odor and independently measured stool changes
assessment: Orange is used in an odor challenge. The one-hour stool collection measures genotype-associated bowel changes independently of odor. No raw-orange ingestion comparison.

fit: isolated curcumin and spinal injury locomotor scores
assessment: The SCI experiment measures hind-limb locomotion, histology and related cellular outcomes after isolated curcumin. It provides no symptomatic pain comparison.

fit: rosemary-associated carnosic acid in a mouse injury model
assessment: Carnosic acid is identified as a constituent and tested in a high-fat model using biochemical and tissue measurements. No fresh-rosemary mood outcome is reported.

fit: TEAM-AD fall adverse events and soybean placebo capsule
assessment: Memantine and dual-placebo arms with an oil-containing capsule reported 38 and 48 ordinary fall events. The active-vitamin arms recorded 58 and 64. The trial varied several interventions and reported no serious-falls difference, p=.89.

fit: isolated piperine oral film detection and adaptation
assessment: The original abstract gives detection at about 35 nanomoles and reduced sensitivity under repeated high exposure. The study does not measure piperine released from cracked pepper or a swallowing endpoint.
